MARKET.head: Shanghai wine trader WINEXSH applies for liquidation amid falling fine wine prices
MARKET.summ: Shanghai-based fine wine trader WINEXSH has applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a supplier reporting an unpaid order and Chinese wine media citing complaints from customers unable to collect wines or secure refunds
takeaways: Shanghai Free Trade Zone Wine Exchange, known as WINEXSH, applied for bankruptcy liquidation, per an October 17 notice on China's bankruptcy disclosure platform.
The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court is reviewing the application, which a Sina Finance report says had a hearing on October 29.
A former supplier says an unpaid order and large inventories left WINEXSH exposed as Chinese fine wine prices declined.

MARKET.head: Western Australian wineries sell well at Shanghai consumer and trade festival
MARKET.summ: A two-day Discover Western Australian Festival drew nearly 900 people in Shanghai, with exhibitors reporting stronger-than-expected consumer sales and new business prospects among distributors, restaurants and hotels
takeaways: Discover Western Australia Festival in Shanghai on November 7-8 drew nearly 600 consumers and about 300 trade professionals.
Twenty exhibitors, including 17 wineries from Margaret River and Great Southern, sold wines on site and through Red Note.
Importers and distributors reported unmet demand, with Xanadu, Willoughby Park and 3 Drops drawing buyers despite limited stock.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria partner on three-year Victorian industry projects
MARKET.summ: A new partnership between Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will fund a range of projects across the Victorian wine industry supporting grapegrowers and winemakers.
takeaways: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will co-fund Victorian wine industry projects over three years, aligned with the Victorian Wine Strategy 2025–2030.
The program combines $540,000 in Victorian Government funding with $346,667 in Wine Australia co-investment via its Australian Wine Future Fund.
Projects target sustainability, biosecurity preparedness, data-driven decision making and export capability, delivered through workshops, webinars and benchmarking tools.

MARKET.head: Wine still tops Australian alcohol purchases as drinking declines and spending rises
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: Vypr and Shop! ANZ report finds 55% of Australians buy wine, ahead of spirits at 46% and beer at 44%.
41% of Australians drink less than a year ago or have stopped, while only 6% drink more.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from around 23% a year earlier.

MARKET.head: Marnong Estate releases first Reserve Chardonnay and new Sangiovese rosé
MARKET.summ: Marnong Estate has unveiled its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay as a part its new collection of cool-climate expressions from the estate's Sunbury vineyards. The 2024 Reserve Chardonnay leads the new range which features the 2025 Single Vineyard Chardonnay and 2025 Estate Chardonnay, offering “distinct interpretations of the...
takeaways: Marnong Estate, a Sunbury winery, has released its first-ever Reserve Chardonnay, the 2024 vintage.
The spring range also includes 2025 Single Vineyard and Estate Chardonnays and a 2026 Estate Sangiovese Rosé.
The new releases are sold through independent merchants, the cellar door and the winery's website.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and PGI wines to Chinese buyers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: Twenty-three Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek Chinese importers and distributors at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Chinese customs data show Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's production is exported, and the EU now takes roughly 60% of its wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine packaging shifts to smaller formats as single-person households grow
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined Australian 187mL wine pack sales rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent from 2023-24 to 2025-26, concentrated in Asia-Pacific markets.
Single-person households make up 26 per cent of Australian households, up from 18 per cent in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules restrict vague eco claims on wine labels from September 27
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, known as EmpCo, bans vague claims like "eco-friendly" and unsubstantiated sustainability badges from September 27.
Old stock is not grandfathered, so impacted producers are using stickers or point-of-sale information to correct claims.
Violations face fines of up to four percent of annual turnover, with enforcement left to individual EU member states.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded value as Burgundy's share climbs
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, extending its lead; 2019 and 2020 vintages led by value.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive the top producers.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6%, led by Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia.

CULTURE.head: Guardian columnist champions affordable school-night wines around £12 a bottle
CULTURE.summ:
Five wines that hit the spot without breaking the bank

Last week, I made The One Sauce from the new Ottolenghi book, Simple Too, and it might well be the zenith of tomato sauces. We ate this gloriously garlicky, vinegar-spiked number with...
takeaways: Columnist argues midweek 'school-night' wine offers impromptu pleasure, arguing against an over-scheduled, all-or-nothing culture.
She sets the budget at about £12 a bottle, noting roughly £7 of that is the wine itself after VAT and duty.
Picks include Berry Bros & Rudd fino at £13.50, M&S Found Encruzado at £8.50 and Cuvée Alice 2023 at £12.45.

CULTURE.head: AI's energy, e-waste and water footprint threatens wine's green image
CULTURE.summ: The Australian and New Zealand wine sector prides itself on sustainability. The very concept has become the industry’s bread and butter, quite frankly. Look at any winery website and you’ll find a dedicated page filled with paragraphs detailing all the initiatives reducing carbon emissions, saving water and limiting energy use...
takeaways: Australian and New Zealand wine has built its reputation on sustainability, but AI-generated content used in its marketing and labels could damage that image.
Training one large language model can emit around 300,000 kg of CO₂, roughly equal to 105 cars each driven 15,000 km a year.
Global e-waste reached 62 million tonnes in 2022, with only 17.4% officially collected and recycled as of 2020 estimates.

CULTURE.head: Marlborough viticulturist Anna Kelland wins 2026 Young Horticulturist of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland has won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title, having “excelled” in an intensive two-day competition in Auckland from 4-5 November. Kelland was the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year and therefore went through to represent the viticulture sector in this year’s...
takeaways: Anna Kelland, a viticulture technician for Constellation Brands in Marlborough, won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title in Auckland, 4-5 November.
The two-day competition against four horticulture peers included practical, technical, business and sustainability challenges plus an innovation project.
Kelland also won three awards and prizes worth more than $25,000, and she is the tenth Young Viticulturist to take the title.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts this episode of the VinePair podcast Wine 101, featuring Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wines.
The conversation covers how Smith Story came to work in the wine business.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its Agrochemical and MRL Search app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its free Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google app stores.
The app gives rapid access to information from the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the 'Dog book'.
Users must perform an app update to keep receiving updates, and the AWRI helpdesk can be reached on 08 8313 6600.

NEWSLETTERS.head: An Austrian wine mini-study with seven interesting bottles
NEWSLETTERS.summ: These wines were being poured at the Star Wine List Inspiration Day in Stockholm, November 2026. Mayersistas Pet Nat Zweigelt
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Mayersistas Pet Nat Zweigelt Rosé 2023 from the Kamptal was poured at the Star Wine List Inspiration Day in Stockholm, November 2026.
Loimer Brut Nature Blanc de Blancs Grosse Reserve 2020 from Langenlois spends 36 months on lees and scored 93/100.
Muhr Ried Spitzerberg Obere Roterd 1er 2022 from Carnuntum, a Blaufränkisch, received the highest score in the mini-study at 96/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Sixteen Austrian Wines You Should Try
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delicious recommendations,including old favourites and new discoveries
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Joost Wijn lists Fischer's Sauvignon Blanc St. Anna 2025 at €25, while Weinmoral offers the 2023 vintage at €19.
Franz Hofstätter's declassified Grüner Veltliner from the Achleiten vineyard in the Wachau is described as uncertified organic.
Hajszan Neumann's Grüner Veltliner Natural 2025 is 12% ABV and costs €15 from Lebendige Weine (2023 vintage).

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues that wine critics' main sins are inadequate expertise, undisclosed conflicts of interest, and the very short time spent assessing each wine.
Atkin says critics should be slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, and that American and British models of expertise differ.
Atkin contends that critics owe loyalty only to those paying their bills, so consumers who want better reviews should fund the reviewers they like.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/8/26

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet the Young Winemakers Reshaping Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Meet the young winemakers in the heart of Burgundy who are tending the vines and shaping the future of wine
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: William Whitehead has taken charge of Domaine Michel Rebourgeon in Pommard, a domaine of 4.25 hectares making about 20,000 bottles a year.
Pierre Arcelain runs Domaine Michel Arcelain, where the white wine spends 12 months in a concrete egg.
Arthur Thibert works alongside his father Pierre in Corgoloin, overseeing a new cuverie and more sustainable farming since 2018.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus scans sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction notices and restaurant sales for hard-to-find bottles.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and optional images, and Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available in its network.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relatively new producer in the Bourgueil appellation, part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot makes an entry-level blended cuvée plus single-vineyard wines from his best slope parcels, with two more cuvées parcellaires set to join from 2020.
Revillot, from a Mâconnais family, trained in Dijon and worked at Domaine Drouhin in Oregon and Newton Johnson in South Africa before reaching the Loire.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872 in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, Penedès, Catalonia.
Cava's name comes from the cellars dug to store the wine, informally used from the 1960s and formalized under Spanish law in 1972.
Cava Gran Reserva requires at least 30 months of lees ageing; the featured Sumarroca 2022 Gran Reserva Brut Nature costs $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with Guangzhou scheduled for November 6, to promote Spanish value wines in China.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Piqueras' El Abuelo, a blend of Alicante Bouschet, Monastrell and Syrah, impressed the author with elegance and judicious oak use for its price.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks drop back on Sunday, marking the start of what she calls Kitchen Season.
Kitchen Season runs through November and December, when cooking shifts toward festive cooking for others and new recipes.
Maker shares a list of kitchen tools she uses year-round, saying none are affiliate links.
